newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS' KOVALEV HURTS KNEE, MAY MISS REST OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS' KOVALEV HURTS KNEE, MAY MISS REST OF SEASON.

text.p: New York Rangers right winger Alexei Kovalev suffered possible ligament damage to his right knee in Wednesday's 4-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning and may be sidelined for the rest of the season.
"The best case scenario is if it's a second-degree sprain of the ligament (anterior cruciate ligament), then it's probably four to six weeks," said Rangers trainer Jim Ramsay.
"Worst case scenario is if it's a complete tear, then probably four months minimum."

Kovalev got tangled up with Tampa Bay's Alexander Selivanov behind the New York goal late in the second period and fell awkwardly to the ice. He was down on the ice for several minutes before he was helped off by trainers.

"The doctor told me it may be the same type of injury as Pavel Bure," said Kovalev, 23, in reference to the Vancouver winger who had knee surgery and missed virtually all of the 1995-96 season. "Right now, it feels loose inside my knee."

Rangers captain Mark Messier said: "The kid (Kovalev) was in tears, he loves to play hockey. It's a devastating feeling. Now that he's out of the lineup, people will see how valuable and underappreciated he is. It's a huge hole to fill."
The Rangers are currently in third place in the Atlantic Division with a 22-17-6 record.

Kovalev, in his fifth year with New York, has 13 goals and 22 assists in 45 games with a plus-11 rating this season. He was the 15th overall selection in the 1991 entry draft, making him the first Soviet player ever taken in the first round.
In 315 games, Kovalev has 93 goals and 122 assists for 215 points. He was instrumental in the Rangers capturing the Stanley Cup in 1994, compiling nine goals and 12 assists in 23 playoff games.
